# Policymaker #205, iteration 0024, pass 5

The challenge fixtures are on main. Session #209 used codex gpt-6.1-sol only (91k input, 7 turns). Its sha256-only Verification passed and the owner accepted the change (request #211) ([report](history/sessions/209/f712e8539fb3deab933bde6fdf60aac2aa6d46254c29bb8c8035ba4e56d19bf3.md)).
I ran the evaluator on main `2e1422c`: exit 0, `errors: []`, `missing: ["baseline"]`, 45 references. Challenges are `prepared-not-reviewed`.
Reviewer #210 ended `blocked` with no report, and its tag has no diff, the same result as #208. The cause is unconfirmed. My working guess: the reviewer profile has `write: []`, and both sessions started from task branches whose `benchmark/` changes were not yet on main. The session protocol says a change outside a role's write paths is refused at merge and the task ends `blocked`.
Change: I deleted the one-off `execution/scripts/land_challenges_195.py` now that the landing has merged.
[Orders](orders.json) (wake false): `review-challenges-main` (reviewer, medium effort, 60 min, 40 turns). It starts from main (`start_branch` null), so its branch has no inherited diff. It writes its report first, checks every evidence pointer with a script, runs both checks itself and ends with accept or revise tied to `2e1422c`.
Expected gain: a substantive review verdict before any scorer work. The next iteration's Policymaker reads the findings and the reviewer's actual `models` block. The author #195 was mostly codex, so a codex review would not count as model-family diverse.
I updated [policy memory](../policy/working-memory.md) with the landing result, the guessed cause of the blocked reviews and the next steps. Routing is unchanged.
Still missing: baseline, native fidelity evidence, typedef-impact and diagram-difference cases, a real split allocation, a scorer and an independent challenge review. Product quality is unmeasured. Pinned fixtures and green structural checks establish neither benchmark readiness nor challenge execution.

## Discoveries
Two reviewer sessions that started from unmerged task branches both ended `blocked` with no report ([pass record in issue #205](../.session/issue.md)). The cause is unconfirmed.

## What next
If the review from main also blocks, read its issue comments and record before re-ordering, and consider a reviewer profile fix or an engine-change.
If it says revise, order benchmark fixes. If it says accept, order scorer design through the evaluator role plus a separate evaluator-verifier.
Do not land the challenge fixtures again; they are on main.

Waiting for the iteration to continue: then `policy/` merges and the orders start.
